knownIssues.summary: Clicking Publish/Unpublish as a caller who is NOT the cycle's direct MyManager (org-hierarchy "Director", two levels above the assessed person - a different authorization class from the feature's own "Director"/evaluator role) throws an unhandled server exception (HTTP 500 from Service/MgScanService.asmx/SetManagementScanPublishState) instead of a graceful authorization error. STILL PRESENT as of 2026-08-12 - reproduced a third time, unchanged. This org-rollup account is no longer part of the regular per-role performance sweep (see terminologyNote) but this finding stays open until fixed.
knownIssues.reproduction: Log in as the org-level account one level above the evaluator (not the candidate's direct MyManager), open Nine-Grid, Generate, select the candidate's cell, click Publish/Unpublish on their row.
knownIssues.evidence: Response body: {"Message":"There was an error processing the request.","StackTrace":"","ExceptionType":""} - reproduced independently on three separate test runs (2026-08-10 x2, 2026-08-12).
knownIssues.suggestedFix: MgScanService.asmx.cs SetManagementScanPublishState already has an UnAuthorized-result check - the underlying ManagementScanPlayBO.SetPublishState call for a non-authorized caller appears to throw before reaching that check rather than returning a normal ManagementScanSaveResult with Errors=["UnAuthorized"]. Not yet filed as an ADO bug.

knownIssues.area: PDF report view/download - toolbar and row-level (Director role)
knownIssues.summary: Both PDF report generation paths available to the Director (evaluator) now work end-to-end: the Nine-Grid toolbar's Report (PDF) button (2-step: language popup, then Ok) produced a real download (ManagementScanOverviewReport_English_20260812.pdf, ~5.4-9.2s across two attempts), and the per-candidate row's Report (PDF) icon also produced a real download (ManagementScanManagerReport_English_20260812.pdf, ~4.5s). Neither path had been correctly instrumented before this run - the row-level icon test previously matched on a static title="Download PDF" HTML attribute that gets overwritten at runtime by a Knockout token binding, so it always silently reported "not found" rather than actually testing the click. Fixed by matching on the stable .fa-file-pdf icon class instead.
knownIssues.reproduction: Director role: Nine-Grid toolbar Report (PDF) button, and the PDF icon on a Voltooid row's action column.

knownIssues.summary: Unlike Publish, the Kalibirity position-override swatches correctly appear non-actionable for the unauthorized org-rollup account - no data mutation is possible, consistent with ADR-001 authorization intent. (Not re-tested this run since that account is no longer part of the default sweep - carried forward from 2026-08-10/2026-08-12 findings.)

Clicking 'Add New' on the candidate listing intermittently lands on an unrelated 'My Account' tab instead of opening the new-candidate form. Recovered reliably with a retry (re-navigate + re-click) every time it's occurred so far.

Creating a second batch of accounts under the same runStamp (e.g. the standalone validation-only account, created after the director/manager/employee hierarchy) used to silently OVERWRITE results/account-setup-<runStamp>.json instead of merging into it, destroying the earlier accounts' saved credentials and crashing the next script that needed them. Fixed 2026-08-12 to merge by role instead of overwriting.

Manager (assessed person) Personal Dashboard PDF: 6,589ms. Director (evaluator) toolbar overview PDF: ~5.4-9.2s across two runs. Director row-level PDF: 4,491ms. All in the same rough range - PDF generation server-side appears to dominate regardless of which surface triggers it.

terminologyNote: Reported roles are the feature's own two-role model ONLY - "Manager" (the person being assessed) and "Director" (their evaluator) - per explicit instruction that this report should not include a third "Employee" category. Underlying test-account naming (for anyone reading the raw scripts/JSON) still uses org-hierarchy names: the account scripted as "employee" plays the assessment and is shown here as Manager; the account scripted as "manager" is the evaluator and is shown here as Director. A third org-hierarchy account (scripted as "director", one level above the evaluator) exists only to demonstrate the Publish/Unpublish 500 bug in Known Issues and is intentionally not included as a timed role in this report.
